known.title: Step 3 Files cell omits the run summary template that the step must change
known.description: Step yolo_teardown's Task adds `### Kept resources` to the run summary template and removes the merged local branch from After merge. Its Files cell lists only `plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/yolo/SKILL.md` and omits `plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/yolo/references/run-summary.md`, which exists at the repo ref. Acceptance A4 also requires that file to contain 'Kept resources'. The plan contract requires Files cells to cover the intended scope, and the code reviewer flags changed paths outside the Steps Files cells.

known.title: No plugin gate row although the repository requires it for a single-plugin change
known.description: The root AGENTS.md says that before committing or pushing a change owned by exactly one plugin, the agent must run `node scripts/ci.mjs --plugin <name>`, the authoritative gate. The plan's own Research (Repository facts, Validators) names `node scripts/ci.mjs --plugin plan-lifecycle` as the plugin's validator set: skill guard, no-author-scripts, agent score, selftest, and plan-cli. No Acceptance row and no step runs it. The only remaining checks are a content-hash check and greps.

known.title: A1 passes a flag that content-hash.mjs does not accept
known.description: A1 runs `node scripts/skills/content-hash.mjs --check plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills`. At the repo ref, the script accepts only `<skill-dir>`, `--backfill [root]`, or `--check-only [root]`. Any other first argument is treated as a skill directory, so `--check` makes hashSkill throw '--check/SKILL.md not found', and the command exits nonzero whatever the hashes are. Step 4's Done when uses the correct `--check-only`.

known.title: Compose fact misstates what `docker compose down` removes by default
known.description: The Compose facts bullet says that `docker compose down` removes anonymous volumes attached to the containers by default, and that `-v` only adds named volumes. The cited Docker reference says 'Anonymous volumes are not removed by default', and `-v, --volumes` removes named and anonymous volumes. The plan's own experiment (both volumes stayed after `down`) and the Compose volumes decision, which lists recorded anonymous volumes under Kept resources, contradict the claim.

known.title: Teardown force-removes a worktree that holds untracked or modified files without a question
known.description: The Worktree delete decision (Research > Decisions), carried into step contract_teardown, retries `git worktree remove --force` when git refuses because of untracked or modified files. The plan justifies this by saying that archive proved the merge and the leftovers are build output. Archive proves only that the reviewed bytes landed. Untracked or modified files in the worktree are unreviewed, unlanded work, and the plan's own experiment shows that the refusal exists to protect them. --force deletes them irrecoverably without in-session confirmation. This contradicts the root AGENTS.md rule against destructive operations without explicit confirmation. The `Merge now` confirmation covers only the stated teardown (`git branch -d`), so it does not authorize this deletion.
